brief: The Market Ear argues the Russell 2000's long-running uptrend is holding, back above its 200-day moving average, though it calls the setup fragile. It cites GS data that positioning is washed out: systematic exposure sits in the 7th percentile and leveraged funds hold record shorts per CFTC data through September 22. Softer PCE and payrolls prints have already triggered some covering, with about $900mn of open interest coming out since September 29 and RTY funding spreads richening outright and versus SPX. The piece says the squeeze fuel is in place and the only missing ingredient is relief in rates. It points to Friday's initial rate decline, which drove an aggressive Russell squeeze that mostly held even after yields reversed higher, leaving Russell diverging from rates. Conclusion: little further relief in rates would be needed to reignite the squeeze, and rates remain the trigger to watch.
